title: Cross Site Scripting (XSS)
definition: XSS occurs when an attacker injects malicious executable JavaScript into a trusted website. When a victim visits the page, their browser executes the script, which can steal session cookies or perform unauthorized actions.
simpleExplanation: Someone writes a script in a public comment box. When you read the comment, the script secretly steals your login cookie and sends it to a hacker.

rows: Malicious payload is saved in the database (e.g. comment section) and served to all users.
Payload is in the URL query string and reflected back on the page by the server.
Client-side JS parses the URL and injects the payload into the DOM unsafely (e.g. using innerHTML).

answers.answer: XSS is a critical architectural pattern in frontend design.

answers.question: What is the main tradeoff of XSS?
answers.answer: Usually a tradeoff between Server CPU usage, TTFB (Time to First Byte), and Client CPU usage.
